haiku-low.q1: Three contiguous breach minutes (M, M-1, M-2), and no unresolved incident already exists for that service and rule.
haiku-low.q2: Each further breach is recorded as an incident_breach row on that incident. No jobs are written and nobody is paged.
haiku-low.q3: Ten consecutive clean minutes, each with trailing 5-minute rate below 1% and requests above zero. A later three-breach streak opens a new incident.
haiku-low.q4: L1 primary at T0, L2 secondary at T0+5m, L3 engineering manager at T0+10m. Due times are fixed when the incident opens.
haiku-low.q5: The page is sent by SMS right away with the same ref. If both fail, it is marked failed, SMS retries 3 times, and the next level still fires.
haiku-low.q6: People recorded in the pages table for the incident get a resolved notice, not the current on-call. Pending page jobs are cancelled, stopping escalation.
haiku-low.q7: In the evaluations table in Postgres. Any non-breach outcome or missing minute resets the breach streak; any non-clean outcome resets the clean streak.
haiku-low.q8: The evaluations primary key on (service, rule, minute) lets only one instance commit each minute. The partial unique index on incidents prevents a second open incident.
haiku-low.q9: Each job's due_at triggers it. The worker checks the incident is still open, then pages the person the schedule service returns at that time.
haiku-low.q10: The provider posts a signed webhook; it is deduplicated via ack_events and marks the incident acknowledged. Pending jobs are cancelled, and claimed jobs drop out on seeing acknowledged.
haiku-low.q11: At the moment the job runs, by querying the schedule service then, falling back to schedule_cache. It is not fixed when the incident opens.
haiku-low.q12: It reads the pages table for that incident, which records who was actually paged, rather than asking who is on call.

sonnet.q1: A breach streak of 3 (breach rows for contiguous minutes M, M-1, M-2, where breach = rate above 2% and at least 500 requests over the trailing 5-minute window) AND no unresolved incident for that (service, rule).
sonnet.q2: No new incident is opened and nobody is paged. Each further breach is recorded as an incident_breach row (I, M) with no jobs created. The partial unique index on unresolved incidents also guards this.
sonnet.q3: It resolves after 10 consecutive minutes (M-9..M) that are all present and all clean (at least 1 request and rate below 1%). Any non-clean or missing minute restarts the clean streak. Zero-request minutes are not clean. There is no manual resolve. After resolution, a later streak of 3 breaches opens a new incident, because the partial index ignores resolved rows.
sonnet.q4: L1 primary at T0 (when the incident opens), L2 secondary at T0+5m, L3 engineering manager at T0+10m. Due times are fixed at open. Ack cancels the pending levels.
sonnet.q5: If push fails or gets no answer within 10 s, the page is sent by SMS right away with the same ref. If both fail, the page is marked failed, SMS is retried up to 3 times 30 s apart, and a notice goes to ops chat. The next level still fires at its fixed due time.
sonnet.q6: Notices go to the distinct recipients in the pages table for that incident (alice and bob, and carol if paged), not whoever is currently on call. Push, with SMS if push fails. Pending page jobs are cancelled on resolution, which stops escalation.
sonnet.q7: In the Postgres evaluations table (one row per service, rule, minute with outcome). Streaks are computed from these rows. Any outcome other than breach (or a missing minute) resets the breach streak. Any outcome other than clean resets the clean streak. unknown (failed metrics query) resets both.
sonnet.q8: The evaluations table has a primary key on (service, rule, minute), so only one instance can commit a minute and the other gets a unique violation, rolls back and skips that minute. A partial unique index on incidents (service, rule) WHERE status <> 'resolved' is a second guard against two open incidents. There is no leader election.
sonnet.q9: Each step is a durable job row in the jobs table, written when the incident opens and due at T0, T0+5m and T0+10m. Workers in both instances poll every 5 s and claim due jobs with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED (60 s lease). The worker locks the incident, checks status=open, inserts the page row (unique per incident and level), and re-checks the incident is still open just before sending. If it is no longer open (acknowledged), it drops the job.
sonnet.q10: The paging provider POSTs a webhook (with ref=incident-level and an event id) to the ack webhook, which runs in both instances. It verifies the signature, inserts the event id into ack_events (a conflict means already handled), locks the incident and sets status=acknowledged WHERE status=open, then marks the incident's pending jobs cancelled, all in one commit. It returns 200 OK. A worker that already claimed a job finds the incident acknowledged and drops it.
sonnet.q11: When the level's job runs, the worker asks the schedule service who holds the role (primary, secondary or manager) at that moment. It falls back to schedule_cache if the service is slow or down, flagging the page stale if the cache is older than the last 09:00 handover. It is not decided when the incident opens. With no answer at all, the level counts as a failed page and the next level fires on time.
sonnet.q12: Resolution inserts notice jobs, one per distinct recipient in the incident's rows in the pages table. Workers claim the notice jobs and record a notice, unique on (incident, recipient). The notices go to the people in the pages table.
